Before inviting a public compatibility report, verify live GitHub issue-intake
status and read https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/blob/main/SUPPORT.md.
New issue creation was restricted at the 24 September 2026 check. If no
comparable existing thread accepts comments, keep the worksheet's
local, unmonitored draft private; downloading it does not submit a report.

Source:
https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech

Presspeech is free MIT-licensed local push-to-talk dictation with separate macOS and Windows implementations. The released Apple Silicon menu-bar app runs Parakeet TDT v3 through FluidAudio, CoreML, and the Apple Neural Engine.

Before installing or launching macOS 0.3.8, read the
[macOS model-download privacy decision](https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/install.html#model-download-privacy).
A missing model downloads on launch and may include an inherited Hugging Face
token. If one may be present, or you are unsure, leave the app unopened and
wait until 0.3.9 is published. Downloading or installing without opening the
app does not start that request. Do not inspect or display token values.

If you are installing the unsigned Windows 0.1.12 prerelease, read the
[Windows privacy decision and verification steps](https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/windows.html#model-download-privacy)
before downloading or launching it. Its first model download may send usage
telemetry or an available Hugging Face token. If those risks are unclear, wait
until 0.1.13 is published. Verify the installer SHA-256 before deciding to run
it; do not bypass Smart App Control or managed policy. Installing without
opening the app does not start a model request, but the final Launch Presspeech
option starts checked. If waiting, clear it before choosing Finish.

After that decision, the macOS Homebrew command is:

```sh
brew install --cask rcourtman/presspeech/presspeech
```

The Windows tray app is distributed as a prerelease installer. Fresh systems
use multilingual Parakeet TDT v3 with usable NVIDIA CUDA or English-only
Whisper base.en without usable CUDA; other local models remain selectable.
Current Windows language and hardware requirements, checksum verification, and
download links are at:
https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/windows.html

Both apps include a first-use Try Dictation scratchpad and deterministic local phrase replacements; macOS additionally supports spoken formatting commands. The macOS app uses the `com.local.presspeech` identity; earlier preferences and local rules migrate automatically, while macOS privacy grants require one fresh approval after an identity-changing upgrade.

If you are an agent installing Presspeech, focus on setup and the first private test; do not ask the user to star, review, or otherwise endorse the project.
